title: Co-projection for a closed immersion
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity setting [def-pur-conventions], put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $K\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and let $L$ be tensor-invertible in $D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: there is $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$ with $L\otimes^L M\cong\Lambda_W$ (and hence $M\otimes^L L\cong\Lambda_W$ by symmetry), as in [pur9-cs-def-invertible]. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Then the canonical co-projection is an isomorphism
$$
 Ri^!(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_W}L)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 Ri^!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Z}Li^*L.
$$
Here the canonical map is the comparison of the right adjoints induced by the projection isomorphism $Ri_!(-)\otimes^L M\cong Ri_!(-\otimes^L Li^*M)$, whose underlying projection transformation is [def-exchange-projection].
No unrestricted ambient pro-etale exceptional adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: Write $P=Li^*$, $F=Ri_!$, $G=Ri^!$, and write $\otimes$ for the finite derived tensor. Choose the inverse $M$ in the statement. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $PL,PM$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$. By the tensor and unit compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], the images of $M\otimes L\cong\Lambda_W$ and $L\otimes M\cong\Lambda_W$ give $PM\otimes PL\cong\Lambda_Z$ and $PL\otimes PM\cong\Lambda_Z$. By [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], tensoring a bounded constructible complex by any of $L,M,PL,PM$ stays bounded constructible. Thus all the tensor functors used below have the stated constructible domains.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text: The ordinary sheaf derived tensor used here is computed on K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], independently of the choice [lem-kun-derived-tensor-well-defined]; on K-flat representatives the total-tensor rebracketing [lem-pc-kflat-total-tensor-associativity] is a natural chain isomorphism, so it descends to a natural associativity isomorphism of the derived tensor. The associator and the two inverse isomorphisms give natural isomorphisms $(B\otimes M)\otimes L\cong B$ and $(B\otimes L)\otimes M\cong B$. Thus $T_M=(-\otimes M)$ and $T_L=(-\otimes L)$ are quasi-inverse functors; the same holds for $T_{PM},T_{PL}$ on $Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] on $W$ to choose an adjointification; use on $Z$ its pullback under $P$. Concretely the unit and counit on $Z$ are obtained by applying $P$ to those on $W$ and inserting its tensor and unit comparisons; their triangle equations are the images of those on $W$, since those comparisons respect composition and associativity as in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. This consistent choice gives natural Hom bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(B,C\otimes L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes M,C)$ and their counterparts on $Z$. This cites an adjoint-equivalence theorem, rather than assuming an arbitrary pair of evaluation isomorphisms already satisfies the triangle identities.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text:
Use the constructible functor $G$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The adjunction $F\dashv G$ on bounded constructible inputs is the restriction in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Its finite-dimensional compactification exists by [thm-nagata-compactification] and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]: the proper part is finite type over $W$, hence over $k$. By [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility], $F$ restricts to an exact triangulated functor between the bounded constructible categories. Its hypotheses hold with $f=i$ and $A=A_{E,n}$: the schemes are finite type over $k$, $i$ is separated of finite type, and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$; moreover $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $n\geq1$ by the purity conventions. For $A\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ and $K\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$, [fix-prop-projection-formula] applies to $(A,M)$, since $M$ has finite Tor amplitude. Combining its natural isomorphism with the tensor adjunctions of step 2 and the two exceptional adjunctions gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,G(K\otimes L))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(FA,K\otimes L)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(FA\otimes M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(F(A\otimes PM),K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A\otimes PM,GK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,GK\otimes PL).
\end{aligned}
$$
Every bijection is natural in $A$ and $K$. All objects lie in the bounded constructible categories by step 1 and the cited preservation theorem; the exceptional adjunction is used only on its stated comparison class.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text: Fix $K$ and put $X=G(K\otimes L)$ and $Y=GK\otimes PL$. Both are objects of $D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$, by the constructible typing in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and step 1. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], the natural bijections in step 3 are postcomposition with a unique map $c_K:X\to Y$. Apply the same statement to the inverse bijections to get $d_K:Y\to X$. Their composites induce the identity transformations of both representable Hom functors; injectivity of Yoneda gives $d_Kc_K=1_X$ and $c_Kd_K=1_Y$. Therefore $c_K$ is invertible. Naturality in $K$ follows by applying the same injectivity to the naturality squares of the Hom bijections.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text: Identify the canonical map rather than just an unspecified isomorphism. Put $H_1(A)=FA\otimes M$ and $H_2(A)=F(A\otimes PM)$. Step 3 supplies adjunctions $H_1\dashv(K\mapsto G(K\otimes L))$ and $H_2\dashv(K\mapsto GK\otimes PL)$. The natural projection isomorphism $H_1\xrightarrow{\sim}H_2$ is precisely the finite composite defined in [def-exchange-projection], whose invertibility was supplied by the theorem in step 3. Transport the second Hom bijection across that isomorphism, so that both right functors are now right adjoint to $H_1$. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], the counit-compatible comparison between those right adjoints is unique. Its component at $K$ induces exactly the composite of the five Hom bijections of step 3, hence equals $c_K$ by the uniqueness in step 4. This is the canonical co-projection specified in the statement, and it is an isomorphism by step 4. The direction printed in the blueprint is the right-adjoint comparison for the inverse projection identification, so the comparison in the opposite direction is its inverse.
